16: /-! ## Old Expressions in Strata Core
17: 
18: The `old e` expression in Strata Core follows the syntax of the old expression
19: in Boogie. Specifically, in Section 4.3 in "This is Boogie 2":
20: 
21: "Postconditions and procedure implementations are two-state contexts. This means
22: that it is possible to refer to two different values of each variable. In a
23: postcondition, the two states are the pre- and post-states of the procedure's
24: invocations, and in a procedure implementation, the two states are the pre-state
25: of the procedure and the current state. In both cases, the pre-state value of an
26: expression is denoted by enclosing it as the argument to `old`. For example, in
27: the postcondition of a procedure, if `x` and `y` are global variables, then
28: `old(x + y)` refers to the value of `x + y` on entry to the procedure, whereas
29: `x + y` not enclosed inside any old expression denotes the value of `x + y` on
30: exit from the procedure.
31: 
32: Only global variables are affected by `old` expressions. For example, if `a` is
33: a global variable, `b` is a local variable, and `c` is an out-parameter, then
34: the use of `old(a + b + c)` in a procedure implementation is equivalent to
35: `old(a) + b + c`. Stated differently, `old` distributes to the leaves of
36: expressions and is the identity for every leaf expression that is not a global
37: variable. Nested occurrences of `old` do not further change the meaning of the
38: expression; `old(old(E))` is equivalent to just `old(E)`. In other words, `old`
39: is idempotent."
40: 
41: In our implementation, function `normalizeOldExpr` removes redundant
42: applications of `old` and distributes `old` to the leaf variables of an
43: expression. Let us suppose we have normalized the body and postconditions of a
44: procedure `P`. No `old` expressions are allowed in `P`'s preconditions. Now we
45: are only left with `old(var)` expressions:
46: 
47: 1. Any `old(var)` in `P`'s body and postconditions can be replaced by the
48:    initial value of `var` (i.e., at the beginning of `P`).
49: 
50: 2. Any `old(var)` in the postcondition of a procedure `Q` that is called in `P`
51:    can be replaced by the value of `var` immediately before `Q`'s call.
52: -/

85:   | .quant _ _ _ _ _ | .app _ _ _ | .ite _ _ _ _  | .eq _ _ _ =>

88: inductive IsFvar : Expression.Expr → Prop where
89:   | fvar : IsFvar (.fvar () v ty)
90:

92:   match He : e with

94:   | .op _ _ _ | .const _ _ | .bvar _ _ | .abs _ _ _
95:   | .quant _ _ _ _ _ | .app _ _ _ | .ite _ _ _ _  | .eq _ _ _ =>

97: /--
98: Normalize an expression containing applications of the `old` function by
99: distributing it to the leaf variables of an expression and by removing nested
100: occurrences.
101: 
102: E.g., `old(a + b + c) == old(a) + old(b) + old(c)` and `old(old(g)) == old(g)`.
103: -/
104: def normalizeOldExpr (e : Expression.Expr) (inOld : Bool := false)
105:   : Expression.Expr :=
106:   match _He : e with
107:   | .fvar _ v ty =>
108:     if inOld then
109:       @oldVar e.metadata e.metadata e.metadata none v ty -- ignoring the operation type
110:     else e
111:   | .const _ _ | .bvar _ _ | .op _ _ _ => e
112:   | .abs m ty e' => .abs m ty (normalizeOldExpr e' inOld)
113:   | .quant m qk ty tr' e' => .quant m qk ty (normalizeOldExpr tr' inOld) (normalizeOldExpr e' inOld)
114:   | .app m e1 e2 =>
115:     match _He1 : e1 with
116:     | .op m o ty =>
117:       if _Hop : o = "old" then
118:         -- is an old var or old expr
119:         match _He2 : e2 with
120:         | .fvar _ _ _ => e
121:         | e' => normalizeOldExpr e' true
122:       else
123:         .app m (normalizeOldExpr e1 inOld) (normalizeOldExpr e2 inOld)
124:     | _ => .app m (normalizeOldExpr e1 inOld) (normalizeOldExpr e2 inOld)
125:   | .ite m c t f => .ite m (normalizeOldExpr c inOld)
126:                       (normalizeOldExpr t inOld) (normalizeOldExpr f inOld)
127:   | .eq m e1 e2 => .eq m (normalizeOldExpr e1 inOld) (normalizeOldExpr e2 inOld)
128:     termination_by sizeOf e
129:   decreasing_by
130:     all_goals simp [sizeOf, Lambda.LExpr.sizeOf]; try simp_all; omega

132: def normalizeOldExprs (sm : List Expression.Expr) :=
133:   sm.map normalizeOldExpr
134: 
135: def normalizeOldCheck (c : Procedure.Check) : Procedure.Check :=
136:   { c with expr := normalizeOldExpr c.expr }
137: 
138: def normalizeOldChecks (c : ListMap String Procedure.Check) : ListMap String Procedure.Check :=
139:   c.map (λ p ↦ (p.fst, normalizeOldCheck p.snd))

142: Checks if `e` contains an application of the `old` function.
143: 
144: This function is agnostic of old expression normalization (see
145: `normalizeOldExpr`). Also see `extractOldExprVars` that extracts `var` from
146: `old(var)` after normalization.
147: -/
148: def containsOldExpr (e : Expression.Expr) : Bool :=
149:   match e with
150:   | .op _ (CoreIdent.unres "old") _ => true
151:   | .op _ _ _ => false
152:   | .const _ _ | .bvar _ _ | .fvar _ _ _ => false
153:   | .abs _ _ e' => containsOldExpr e'
154:   | .quant _ _ _ tr' e' => containsOldExpr tr' || containsOldExpr e'
155:   | .app _ e1 e2 => containsOldExpr e1 || containsOldExpr e2
156:   | .ite _ c t f => containsOldExpr c || containsOldExpr t || containsOldExpr f
157:   | .eq _ e1 e2 => containsOldExpr e1 || containsOldExpr e2

159: /--
160: Get a list of original global variable names that are referred to in an
161: `old(...)` expression. Note that `expr` below should be normalized by
162: `normalizeOldExpr`.
163: -/
164: def extractOldExprVars (expr : Expression.Expr)
165:   : List Expression.Ident := match expr with
166:   | .const _ _ | .bvar _ _ | .fvar _ _ _ | .op _ _ _ => []
167:   | .abs _ _ e => extractOldExprVars e
168:   | .quant _ _ _ tr e => extractOldExprVars tr ++ extractOldExprVars e
169:   | .app _ e1 e2 => match e1, e2 with
170:     | .op _ (CoreIdent.unres "old") _, .fvar _ v _ => [v]
171:     | .op _ (CoreIdent.unres "old") _, _ => panic! s!"Old expression {expr} not normalized"
172:     | e1', e2' => extractOldExprVars e1' ++ extractOldExprVars e2'
173:   | .ite _ c t e => extractOldExprVars c ++ extractOldExprVars t ++ extractOldExprVars e
174:   | .eq _ e1 e2 => extractOldExprVars e1 ++ extractOldExprVars e2
175: 
176: /--
177: Substitute `old(var)` in expression `e` with `s`.
178: -/

180:   Expression.Expr :=

185:   | .app m e1 e2 =>
186:     match e1, e2 with
187:     | .op _ (CoreIdent.unres "old") _, .fvar _ x _ =>
188:       -- NOTE: We rely on the typeChecker to normalize `e` ensure that `old` is
189:       -- only used with an `fvar`.
